newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says it will seek to change Helms-Burton law.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says it will seek to change Helms-Burton law.

text.p: The Clinton Administration said on Friday it would seek to change the Helms-Burton law on Cuba as part of an agreement with the European Union to defuse a trade dispute at the World Trade Organisation.
But a spokesman for one of the law's sponsors, Senator Jesse Helms, said the North Carolina Republican would oppose any changes that would weaken the legislation's major provisions.

As part of the deal, the United States and the EU pledged to develop a common policy to deter foreign investments in assets expropriated in contravention of international law, U.S. Commerce Undersecretary Stuart Eizenstat told a news conference.

"Our goal in this endeavour is to globalize strong standards fo the enhanced protection of property rights," Eizenstat said, adding that the two parties would try to reach a final agreement by Oct. 15.

In the meantime, the White House will seek an amendment to the law to give Clinton authority to waive a provision barring executives of companies that invest in disputed properties in Cuba from entering the United States.

Clinton, who enacted the law last year after Cuba shot down two small U.S. civilian aircraft, has already twice waived another provision that would allow U.S. citizens to sue foreigners for doing business with confiscated property in Cuba.
